title: What Does a Zoom Actually Add? Decomposing Fine-Grained Perception Failures in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.26904v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Zooming into a region often turns a wrong answer from a vision-language model (VLM) into a right one, and a growing literature takes this as evidence that the model lacked the pixels. But a zoom changes several things at once. It removes the surrounding context, re-tokenizes, at a higher density, pixels the model has already seen, and, if the first pass was downsampled, exposes detail the model never received. We separate these factors for each failure. Holding the first pass fixed, we vary only the second look and assign every failure to the cheapest one that fixes it: reusing cached tokens, isolating the region, re-tokenizing the seen pixels, or acquiring new ones. The study covers 2,753 zoom-rescued failures of Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and InternVL3 on V*, ZoomBench and TextVQA, at first-pass budgets from 17x fewer pixels than the source to native resolution. translated_title: 缩放究竟增加了什么？分解视觉-语言模型中的细粒度感知失败
translated_abstract: 将某个区域放大（zoom）往往能把视觉-语言模型（VLM）的错误答案变成正确答案，越来越多的文献将此视为模型缺乏像素信息的证据。但缩放会同时改变几件事：它移除了周围的上下文，以更高的密度对模型已经看过的像素进行重新分词，并且如果第一遍处理时进行了降采样，它还会暴露模型从未接收过的新细节。我们为每一个失败案例分离出这些因素。在保持第一遍处理固定不变的情况下，我们只改变第二次观察，并将每个失败归因于能修复它的最廉价方案：重用缓存的token、隔离目标区域、对已看过的像素重新分词，或获取新的像素。该研究涵盖了Qwen2.5-VL、Qwen3-VL和InternVL3在V*、ZoomBench和TextVQA上的2,753个被缩放拯救的失败案例，第一遍的像素预算从比源图像少17倍到原生分辨率不等。首先，大多数被拯救的失败并非因为缺乏像素：对已看过的像素进行上采样（摘要内容此处截断）
tldr: 该研究将缩放操作分解为多个独立因素，发现大多数VLM被缩放拯救的细粒度感知失败并非因为缺少像素信息，而主要源于对已看像素的重新分词等处理环节。
en_tdlr: By decomposing zoom operations into separate factors, this study reveals that most zoom-rescued fine-grained perception failures in vision-language models stem not from missing pixels but from the re-tokenization of already-seen pixels.
